gumtree_entries.description:
ADDED i2: Tests for {@link Nysiis}, the NYSIIS phonetic encoder.

The encoder first cleans the input (keeping only letters, upper-casing them) and then applies the NYSI
ADDED i3: In non-strict mode the encoded value is not truncated, so the full 8-character NYSIIS code is returned.
ADDED i4: The same input as above but with the default (strict) encoder, whose output is capped at 6 characters.
ADDED i5: Encoding a value via the generic {@code encode(Object)} method does not change the encoder's configured strict mode.
ADDED i6: An empty input is encoded without altering the encoder's strict mode.
ADDED i7: A {@code null} input is handled gracefully and the encoder remains strict.
ADDED i8: {@code encode(Object)} rejects arguments that are not Strings by throwing an exception originating from {@link Nysiis}.
ADDED i10: {@code encode(Object)} accepts a String argument and returns its NYSIIS code.
ADDED i11: Punctuation and digits are stripped before encoding, leaving only the letters to drive the NYSIIS code.
ADDED i12: Mixed-case input with embedded symbols is upper-cased and cleaned before being encoded.
ADDED i13: A longer mixed-case input is truncated to 6 characters in strict mode.
ADDED i14: The {@code encode(String)} method produces the same NYSIIS code as {@link Nysiis#nysiis(String)}; the "KSCH" prefix collapses to a single "C".
ADDED i15: Input containing braces and other symbols is cleaned to its letters and encoded to a 6-character code.
ADDED i16: Another mixed-case input with symbols encodes to a 6-character code.
ADDED i17: {@code encode(String)} cleans whitespace and symbols before encoding.
